question.text: This second president of the US was the only president ever officially elected as a Federalist.
question.answerHtml: John Adams [do not accept or prompt on “John Quincy Adams”]
question.clue: This man's wife asked him to "remember the ladies."

swap.text: The issue of the "midnight judges" led to this 1803 Supreme Court Case that struck down the Judiciary Act of 1789 and established the principle of judicial review.
swap.clue: This case decided it was "emphatically the province and duty of the judicial department" to deny to issue a writ of mandamus to the plaintiff, who was appointed as a Justice of the Peace.

question.leadin: The Wilmot Proviso attempted to outlaw slavery in any territories gained during this conflict.
question.text: Name this war between neighboring countries that ended in 1848 with the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo.
question.clue: A young Abraham Lincoln challenged this war in the Spot Resolutions.

swap.leadin: Territory gained through it was explored by Lewis and Clark.
swap.text: Name this 1803 transaction in which the United States gained the namesake territory from France.
swap.clue: Saint Louis's Three Flags Day ceremony saw Spain turn over the involved assets to another empire, who relinquished the land the next day.

question.text: This 1787 revolt showed the need for a strong central government. During this revolt, Massachusetts veterans led an unsuccessful attack on the Springfield Armory.
question.clue: It ended with a defeat at Petersham, after which its leader fled to Vermont, as Governor James Bowdoin fielded an army led by Benjamin Lincoln and William Shepard.

swap.leadin: It included large portions of southern Arizona and New Mexico, and cities such as Tucson and Sierra Vista.
swap.text: Name this 1854 agreement between U.S. and Mexico, which enabled the construction of a transcontinental railroad.
swap.clue: Its namesake served under Andrew Jackson during the War of 1812 before becoming president of the South Carolina Railroad Company.

question.leadin: The unpopularity of these laws contributed to Thomas Jefferson's win in 1800.
question.text: Name these laws that were passed amid fear of a war with France. One of these laws, the Naturalization Act, increased the residency requirement for citizenship from 5 years to 14 years.
question.clue: These laws required a 14-year pre-residency requirement before immigrants could become citizens.

swap.text: Some of the Cherokee signed this treaty in 1835, although none of their chiefs agreed. This treaty, named after the last Cherokee capital, ceded their land to the US.
swap.clue: It was steadfastly opposed by John Ross, and the group that was involved in it, known as the "Ridge Party," was in violation of the law.

question.leadin: Following this battle, the Americans destroyed an Indian settlement at Moraviantown and broke a coalition that had earlier fought at Tippecanoe.
question.text: Identify this victory for William Henry Harrison fought in Ontario during the War of 1812.
question.clue: This United States victory built on success at the Battle of Lake Erie.

swap.leadin: On June 22, 1807, the American ship Chesapeake was overtaken by a British frigate, which fired after demanding to board and seize deserters.
swap.text: This man replaced James Barron as commander of the Chesapeake after the incident and was killed in a duel by Barron. He burned the Philadelphia during the Barbary wars.
swap.clue: Benjamin Latrobe built this man a house in Lafayette Square, where this victor over the Macedonian became a Washington celebrity.

question.leadin: One person with this last name was given command of the New York department of the Continental Army by George Washington.
question.text: Name this surname of the elder of the first two New York senators. A woman with this [emphasize] maiden name helped establish the Graham Windham orphanage following her husband's death by gunshot at Weehawken.
question.answerHtml: Schuyler [or Eliza (beth) Schuyler Hamilton or Philip John Schuyler; reject “Hamilton” alone] (The lead-in refers to Philip John Schuyler, Eliza Schuyler’s father.)

swap.leadin: Answer the following about historically significant American roads.
swap.text: A funding bill for this road situated entirely within Kentucky was controversially vetoed by Andrew Jackson, who allegedly did so to spite his Kentuckian rival Henry Clay.
swap.clue: As part of his rivalry with Clay, Jackson vetoed a bill to fund this proposed road linking Lexington, Kentucky to the namesake city on the Ohio river, limiting the success of the American System.

question.leadin: A popular chengyu ("chung-eww") idiom sums up the 4th century as this many "barbarians" "throwing China into chaos" by founding the Sixteen Kingdoms during the Jin dynasty.
question.text: Give this traditional number of dynasties that later arose alongside "ten kingdoms" between the Tang and Song. The "Celestial Masters" led a Daoist separatist movement named for this many "pecks of rice."
question.answerHtml: five [or wǔ; accept Way of the Five Pecks of Rice or Wǔ Dǒu Mǐ Dào; accept Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms period or Wǔ dài shí guó; accept Five Barbarians or Wǔ Hú or Wǔ Hú luàn Huá]
question.clue: The Roman king of this number was the first Etruscan one and was Tarquinius Priscus.

swap.text: During the war, this American frigate ran aground and was captured by residents of Tripoli, who installed her as a gun battery. In a daring raid, Lieutenant Stephen Decatur destroyed this vessel to deny her use by the enemy.
swap.clue: That mission used the ketch Intrepid and enlisted the skill of the commanding officer from the schooner Enterprise.

question.text: This President of Texas was responsible for moving the Texas archives to Austin. This successor of Sam Houston authorized "redbank" currency, which further exacerbated Texas's debt.

swap.leadin: Benjamin Russell coined the name of this period in 1817.
swap.text: What period took place during James Monroe's presidency and was supposedly a non-partisan era where the country was unified?
swap.clue: This period of American history succeeded the War of 1812. It was characterized by a common sense of nationalism, optimism, and positivity, and coincided with the presidency of James Monroe.

question.leadin: This event saw soldiers onboard the steamboat Warrior murder more than 150 Indians over two days, ignoring a white flag waved on the first day.
question.text: Identify this event that occurred in the aftermath of the Battle of Wisconsin Heights, and involved a militia firing under the command of General Henry Atkinson.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about what happened after the Battle of the Alamo.
swap.text: This two-word term is used to describe the two months in early 1836 after the fall of the Alamo, when native Texans fled from their homes, hastily abandoning settlements like Washington-on-the-Brazos in fear of Santa Anna's army.
swap.clue: Houston's victory at San Jacinto came after this desperate campaign, during which news of the massacres at the Alamo and Goliad caused the provisional government of Texas to flee from Santa Anna's advancing army.

question.leadin: Identify the following relating to a battle FTPE.
question.text: This Kentucky colonel claimed to have killed Tecumseh at the Thames. For his insistence that he did so, he was elected Vice-President in 1837. He is also famous for living openly with a female slave and their mulatto children.
question.clue: During one election, this politician used a slogan that began with the chant "rumpsey dumpsey, rumpsey dumpsey," even though John Catron wrote that "a lucky random shot" did not qualify him for his post.

swap.leadin: Identify the following about battles from the War of 1812.
swap.text: Riall allegedly screamed "Those are Regulars, by God!" when he realized the soldiers under Winfield Scott and Jacob Brown at this battle earlier in July were more well trained than the militia he expected. Riall retreated after losing over 500 men.
